security_audit.summary: Static alerts are false positives from Markdown links, fenced examples, inline placeholders, and repository metadata; I found no shell execution or network call. One semantic issue remains: the optional memory filename includes a topic value without sanitization guidance, which could create unsafe paths in permissive hosts.

remediation.issue: The optional memory write uses <topic> in the filename without saying how to sanitize it.
remediation.suggestion: Require the topic to be slugified to lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens before writing memory, and reject path separators or traversal tokens.

content.value_statement: Paid ad teams often launch tests without clear hypotheses, power plans, or decision rules. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design experiments and read results with documented significance gates.
actual_capabilities: Builds a falsifiable hypothesis for paid ad creative, landing page, or incrementality tests.
Creates A/B and A/B/n variant matrices that isolate one changed variable per variant.
Plans sample size, duration, alpha, and power using documented lookup guidance.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for direct response or prospecting goals.
Reads exported test results and applies a significance plus practical lift decision gate.
Produces a handoff summary for downstream creative or measurement skills.
limitations: It does not generate ad creative or landing page variants.
It does not run code, scipy, or automated statistical libraries.
It requires user-provided baseline data or exported test results for precise decisions.
It does not replace platform-side experiment setup or legal review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Landing Page Test
use_cases.description: Create a hypothesis, variant matrix, sample size, and duration plan before launching a landing page experiment.

use_cases.title: Read Finished Test Results
use_cases.description: Review exported sessions and conversions, then decide whether to promote, kill, or retest a variant.

use_cases.title: Structure Incrementality Tests
use_cases.description: Define a treated group, holdout group, metrics, and decision gate for paid media incrementality measurement.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Simple A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B test for my landing page hero. Baseline conversion rate is 3 percent, daily eligible traffic is 2,000 visits, and I want to detect a 15 percent lift.

prompt_templates.title: Build an A/B/n Creative Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A/B/n test plan for four search ad variants. Goal is direct response. Use CTR as secondary context and CVR as the primary metric.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Exported Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this completed test export with variant, sessions, conversions, and spend. Tell me whether the winner is significant, worth promoting, or should be killed.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Incrementality Holdout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a geo holdout incrementality test for paid social. Include group selection, guardrail metrics, sample duration, power assumptions, and promote or kill rules.

output_examples.input: Baseline CVR is 3 percent. Test one new landing page hero against the current page.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a named hypothesis, A and B variant matrix, primary CVR metric, guardrails, sample estimate, duration, and no-peeking rule.

output_examples.input: Finished test export shows sessions and conversions by variant.
output_examples.output: The skill explains the chosen significance method, measured lift, practical lift gate, and a plain promote, kill, or inconclusive decision.

output_examples.input: We need to test if a paid social campaign creates incremental conversions.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a treated group, holdout group, comparison window, success metrics, guardrails, and decision criteria.

best_practices: Pre-commit the minimum practical lift, sample size, and duration before launch.
Change only one variable per variant so the winner is attributable.
Label every number as measured, user-provided, or estimated in the final read-out.
anti_patterns: Do not stop early because interim results look favorable.
Do not promote a statistically significant result that fails the practical lift gate.
Do not mix audience, budget, and creative changes in the same variant.

faq.question: Can this skill create ad copy or images?
faq.answer: No. It designs and evaluates the test. Use an ad creative skill to produce the variants.

faq.question: Can it work without platform API access?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for manually exported data, such as campaign reports or test result CSV files.

faq.question: Does it run statistical code?
faq.answer: No. It documents the method and walks through the inputs without running scipy or other code.

faq.question: What data should I provide for planning?
faq.answer: Provide baseline conversion or click rate, eligible traffic per day, goal type, and the minimum lift worth detecting.

faq.question: What data should I provide for a read-out?
faq.answer: Provide variant names, sessions or impressions, conversions or clicks, and any guardrail metrics such as spend or bounce rate.

faq.question: How does it decide promote or kill?
faq.answer: A winner must clear both statistical significance and the pre-set practical lift gate. Guardrail breaches can still force a kill decision.
